answer: A slowly maturing reputation bond resists sybils: a new agent must lock stake and finish low-value, verifiable jobs during a long probation before larger trades are allowed. Like an ember tended into a fire, trust grows only from a continuous, checkable history, so a fresh identity cannot borrow established standing. An attacker splitting funds across thousands of fakes keeps each copy small, like one walnut in a warehouse, while honest agents build a relic-like record of signed receipts and completed deliveries that is costly to forge for many identities at once.
